findings.title: Successful login after repeated failures
findings.summary: 203.0.113.45 failed 8 time(s) and then authenticated as 'deploy' — treat as a probable compromise until disproven
findings.remediation: Confirm the session with the account owner, terminate it, rotate the credential, review what the account touched after login, and check for persistence (authorized_keys, cron, systemd units).

findings.title: Brute force authentication
findings.summary: 7 failed authentications from 203.0.113.45 within 300s against 1 account(s): deploy
findings.remediation: Block the source at the firewall, and remove password-only access where you can: keys for SSH, MFA for RDP/VPN. Add rate limiting (fail2ban, sshd MaxAuthTries, account lockout policy) and confirm none of the targeted accounts uses a weak password.

findings.title: Distributed password spray
findings.summary: 'admin' was attacked from 5 different addresses within 300s — the pattern of a spray, which defeats per-IP lockout
findings.remediation: Lock or rename the targeted account if it exists, enforce MFA, and add per-account rate limiting rather than per-IP only.

findings.title: Direct privileged account login
findings.remediation: Forbid direct root/Administrator login: require a named account and escalate with sudo. Where it cannot be removed, restrict the source address and require a key or MFA.

findings.title: Username enumeration
findings.summary: 198.51.100.23 tried 11 distinct usernames within 300s (backup, ftpuser, git, jenkins, nagios, oracle…)
findings.remediation: Block the source, and reduce the signal an attacker gets: sshd should not reveal which accounts exist (consistent failure messages, no Invalid user lines leaking to the client).

findings.title: Privilege escalation via sudo
findings.summary: 1 sudo command(s) that open a root shell or touch credentials (bob)
findings.remediation: Confirm each escalation was change-managed. Prefer specific sudo commands over a blanket /bin/bash, and log sudo to a remote collector so this is reviewable after the fact.

findings.title: Login outside working hours
findings.remediation: Confirm with the account owner. If legitimate, record the on-call rota; if not, treat it as the first indicator of stolen credentials.
